Five things you found after build 15:18 went live. Two are fixed and measured; three need one line from you.

I told you it was done when it was not

You are right to push on this. I tested each item on its own, on a seeded page, in a headless browser — then reported done. You opened the real Edit window and four things were broken. My tests passed because they never did what you actually do.

Two of these five are faults I introduced last round while fixing something else: the calendar lost its stacking order, and my alarm fix wrote to a place that Save overwrites.

What changes: nothing gets reported done until I have driven it in Safari, through the whole path — open, change, save, close, reopen, reload — and looked at the result. Not one step, the whole path.

what else this connects to, before you approve

Items 1 and 2 share a cause with each other and with last round: something writes a value, and something else overwrites it. The calendar, the alarm list and the old flicker are all one shape of bug. I am fixing them as one rule — one owner per thing — rather than three patches.

What I would check next, that you have not asked for: if Save overwrites the alarm list, it may do the same to subtasks and tags, which are built the same way. I want to test those in the same pass rather than wait for you to find them.

And a question worth settling now: a note that is only a picture currently counts as an empty note. Should a picture also show in the Completed and Past due lists the way text notes do? I would say yes, and I will do that unless you say otherwise.

1

The due-date calendar opens BEHIND the notes box

waiting on you

WAITING ON YOU — approve or correct it

Where: the Edit window → Due Date.

"the edit portion for the due date, the calendar is not showing, and I believe it's in the background behind the edit line."

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

You were exactly right, and this one is mine. Measured: the calendar is created — display block, visibility visible, opacity 1, on screen — but asking the browser what is on top at the calendar's own centre returns note-rich, the notes box. It is painted behind it.

Cause: the old code set the calendar's stacking order to the maximum on every tick. When I merged the two fighting positioners into one last round, I kept the position and dropped the stacking order, so it fell back to the stylesheet's 9999 while the dialog sits at 99999.

Fix: the one placer now owns everything about where that panel sits, stacking order included. Verified: the topmost element at the calendar's centre is now a day button inside the calendar.

The picture shows: pressing Due Date on the same task, on your build and on the fix

2

A reminder you save is gone when you go back

waiting on you

WAITING ON YOU — approve or correct it

Where: the Edit window → Reminder → +, then Save.

"I made a reminder and I put a time, I saved it, and then when I go back inside, the alarm is not over there... when I go to the edit thing and add a reminder, I press save, it does not save."

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

Reproduced exactly. Measured through your steps: 1 alarm after pressing +, 1 after Set, and 0 after Save. Save was destroying it.

Cause, and this one is mine too: the dialog keeps its own list of alarms, taken when the window opens, and Save writes that list over the task. My fix last round added the new alarm somewhere else, so Save overwrote it with the stale, empty copy.

Fix: one owner. The dialog's list is the only list, and everything that adds an alarm adds to it. Verified through a full reload: the alarm is still there and the Alarms tab lists it.

The picture shows: the Alarms tab after adding a reminder and pressing Save

4

A picture pasted into notes leaves no trace on the task

waiting on you

WAITING ON YOU — approve or correct it

Where: the Edit window → the notes box.

"regarding adding a picture in notes, it still doesn't work."

what I want to check with you

When you paste, do you see the picture appear in the box at all? If it never appears even for a moment, that is a different fault from the one I measured, and I need to chase Safari's clipboard specifically.

the cause, measured, and how I fix it

Measured: the paste itself does work — the image lands in the box, is stored as part of the note, and is still there after a full reload.

But the task shows no sign of it. The "this task has notes" pen mark is decided by a test that strips every tag out of the note and asks whether any text is left. A note that is only a picture has no text, so it counts as empty and the mark never appears — the task looks exactly as if nothing was pasted.

Fix: a picture is content. The test will count an image as a note, so the pen mark appears and the task no longer looks blank.

The picture shows: the notes box — the defect is on the task row, which shows no pen mark after you paste a picture
